Job Title: Physical Therapist
Job Location: Oklahoma City, OK
Working Hours: 8*5

Position Summary:
The Physical Therapist provides therapeutic treatments under the direction of a physician to support patient recovery, mobility, and overall health outcomes. Working independently with minimal direction, the therapist evaluates patients, develops treatment plans, and delivers evidence-based therapy to achieve short- and long-term goals. This role requires clinical expertise, strong communication skills, and the ability to guide patients in taking responsibility for their rehabilitation.
 
Key Responsibilities:
  • Interpret physician orders, evaluate patients, and formulate treatment plans to meet short- and long-term goals.
  • Assess patient responses to therapy and adjust treatment plans as needed.
  • Participate in discharge planning, including preparing and instructing patients in home exercise programs.
  • Document treatment results and patient progress in medical records.
  • Supervise and assist students during clinical rotations, depending on experience level.
  • Maintain, clean, and ensure proper use of physical therapy equipment.
  • Collaborate effectively with staff, patients, and families to support patient outcomes.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
 
Required Qualifications & Skills:
  • Education: Baccalaureate degree in Physical Therapy.
  • Experience: Entry-level; no prior experience required.
  • Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
  • Knowledge of physical therapy principles, methods, techniques, and equipment.
  • Understanding of anatomy and physiology for patient evaluation and treatment.
  • Ability to adjust and operate therapy equipment based on patient needs.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills to guide and motivate patients.
  • Proficiency with computers and electronic medical records.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships with staff and patients.
 
Required Certifications & Licensure (one of the following):
  • Current license from the Oklahoma Board of Medical Licensure and Supervision as a Physical Therapist.
  • Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from the American Heart Association (required upon hire).
 
Core Competencies:
  • Deliver patient-centered care with empathy and professionalism.
  • Apply physical therapy techniques with accuracy and safety.
  • Adapt treatment plans to changing patient needs.
  • Collaborate effectively within a healthcare team.
  • Maintain thorough documentation and adherence to protocols.
